source.title: LION-DG: Layer-Informed Initialization with Deep Gradient Protocols for Accelerated Neural Network Training

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Appendix D lists the code URL as [ANONYMOUS URL], so no usable repository URL is stated.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares initialization choices and reports their effect on training speed, a conceptual test of V4. It measures time to reach 70% training accuracy, not near-zero training error, so it does not test V1.
record.gate_note: The reported speed measure is time to reach 70% training accuracy. This does not establish whether models reach zero or near-zero training classification error. Gradient-ratio plots describe the proposed method's dynamics but are not the training-error result named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses He and LSUV backbone initialization while evaluating its own auxiliary-head initialization method. Its results concern gradient interference in deeply supervised DenseNet and residual architectures. They do not test V4's activation-matched signal propagation in plain networks, trainable depth, or orthogonal initialization. Initialization-dependent speed alone does not establish that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors attribute faster convergence to initially suppressing auxiliary gradients, report architecture- and dataset-dependent benefits, and recommend LSUV plus LION-DG for DenseNet-DS accuracy. For ResNet-DS, they recommend LSUV for CIFAR-10 accuracy and emphasize LION-DG's CIFAR-100 speed benefit.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention zero-initializes auxiliary classifier heads and uses standard He initialization for the backbone in deeply supervised DenseNet-DS and ResNet-DS; the tested outcome is speed to 70% training accuracy, not the versions' zero-error endpoint.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported speedup varies by architecture and dataset: DenseNet-DS on CIFAR-10, ResNet-DS on CIFAR-10, and ResNet-DS on CIFAR-100 have different outcomes. The paper says the ResNet-DS side-tap design matters.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-initializing auxiliary heads reduces time to 70% training accuracy by 8.3% for CIFAR-10 DenseNet-DS, 3.6% for CIFAR-10 ResNet-DS, and 11.3% for CIFAR-100 ResNet-DS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary-head initialization can accelerate deeply supervised network training by delaying auxiliary gradient contributions, with architecture- and dataset-dependent accuracy trade-offs.

record.code_released: not stated (Appendix D says “Code available at: [ANONYMOUS URL]”)
record.problems: The measured convergence target is 70% training accuracy rather than near-zero training error. Speed results are aggregate averages over 3 seeds; no uncertainty for speedup is stated in the extracted result text. Experiments are limited to CIFAR-scale datasets, as the authors acknowledge.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 compares LSUV and Hybrid as well as LION-DG and He-init. Those method comparisons are not separately extracted because the claim versions do not name those methods; the retained rows capture LION-DG's reported speed outcomes relevant to V4. Table 7 gives Fixup and ReZero per-seed steps to 70% training accuracy but the supplied text does not provide He-init steps for direct comparison.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels; the reported convergence target is 70% training accuracy.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and student overparameterization.
Training-error degradation across depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified initialization recipes.
Activation-matched signal-preserving initialization in plain networks, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, and very deep orthogonal convolutional networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.

Controlled normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup residual networks. Fixup results here concern DenseNet-DS and do not test the residual-network claim.

record.verdict_notes: The reported speedups remain useful method results, but do not warrant verdicts on the supplied versions. Speedup uncertainty is not supplied alongside the three values. LSUV, Hybrid, and Fixup/ReZero comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out; their omission therefore requires no missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels; the study reports speed to 70% training accuracy instead.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Depth sweeps comparing plain networks with identity shortcuts, and the specified special initialization or normalization comparisons.

Whether activation-matched signal-preserving initializations train plain networks faster or at greater depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks; and training plain convolutional networks at 10,000 layers.
Training above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness changes, recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for learning speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: DenseNet-DS
rows.size_stated: Approximately 77K parameters; growth rate k = 12; 3 dense blocks with 6 layers each.
rows.operation_detail: Zero-initialize auxiliary classifier heads while using He initialization for the backbone (LION-DG).
rows.measure: Reduction in time to reach 70% training accuracy (speedup).
rows.note: The paper says results are averaged over 3 seeds; this row records the aggregate reported speedup.
rows.check: The +8.3% speedup is correctly reported, but compares auxiliary-head initialization methods in DenseNet-DS. Backbone He initialization is held fixed; the result does not test V4's signal-preserving initialization mechanism in plain networks.

rows.subject: ResNet-DS
rows.operation_detail: Zero-initialize auxiliary classifier heads while using He initialization for the backbone (LION-DG), with auxiliary heads implemented as side-taps.
rows.measure: Reduction in time to reach 70% training accuracy (speedup).
rows.note: The paper characterizes the CIFAR-10 speedup as modest and reports a slight accuracy trade-off.
rows.check: The +3.6% speedup is correctly reported, but concerns auxiliary-head interference in residual ResNet-DS, outside V4. Validation accuracy falls from 89.42% to 87.18%; this does not qualify a claim version about plain-network signal propagation.

rows.subject: ResNet-DS
rows.operation_detail: Zero-initialize auxiliary classifier heads while using He initialization for the backbone (LION-DG), with auxiliary heads implemented as side-taps.
rows.measure: Reduction in time to reach 70% training accuracy (speedup).
rows.note: The paper reports matching baseline accuracy for this condition.
rows.check: The +11.3% speedup is correctly reported, but concerns auxiliary-head initialization in residual ResNet-DS, outside V4. Matching validation accuracy does not establish the mechanism or plain-network setting named by V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: LION-DG improves speed to the 70% training-accuracy target by +8.3% versus He-init (R1). This supports an initialization-dependent training-speed effect in this tested setup.

reader_labels.reason: The speedup is modest at +3.6%, and the paper reports a slight accuracy trade-off (R2).
